claims.claim: Hong Kong should not impose a hard cap on initial rents.
Hong Kong should tighten tenure security and conditions, plus a light indexed rent band.
The public-housing queue is the real instrument for housing policy.
SDU tenants pay a 15–25 percent per-square-foot premium for the worst housing.
Real rent burden has worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income.
The 2021 ordinance changed nothing Mrs Wong can see.
Mr Chan was evicted with two weeks' notice for requesting a window repair.
The 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance capped increases within a tenancy but left initial rents untouched.
First-generation rent controls show consistent supply contraction, while second-generation controls show small or null stock effects.
The stable SDU stock from 2019 to 2025 is evidence that moderate regulation is survivable, not that a binding cap is safe.
The stability may be an artifact of a non-binding instrument.
The reviewed elasticity of marginal SDU-type supply is 0.31–0.48.
A 10 percent cap-induced cut removes roughly 3–5 percent of stock over five years.
A 15 percent initial-rent cut transfers about HK$900 a month to incumbents while leaving 3,000–4,000 households a year unable to enter the segment.
Berlin's Mietendeckel led to initial-offer rents falling, listing supply contracting, and a backlog of suppressed increases releasing above the pre-cap trend line when struck down.
Inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock annually.
A band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing an estimated 40–60 staff-years.
A cap would systematically miss the most exploited tail of tenants.
The subcommittee could not identify any design under which the newest-arrival tail is protected first rather than last.
61 percent of surveyed households would trade a nominal rent increase for three-year security of tenure, and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer.

cites.sentence: SDU tenants pay a 15–25 percent per-square-foot premium for the worst housing in the city [D1p1], and real rent burden has worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income [D2p2].
SDU tenants pay a 15–25 percent per-square-foot premium for the worst housing in the city [D1p1], and real rent burden has worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income [D2p2].
Mrs Wong, nine years in a unit with no written agreement, says the 2021 ordinance "changed nothing she can see" [D4p1].
Mr Chan's landlord evicted him with two weeks' notice for requesting a window repair [D3p1].
The 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance was second-generation: it capped increases within a tenancy but left initial rents untouched [D1p3].
The academic literature finds first-generation controls (hard caps on levels) show consistent supply contraction, while second-generation controls show small or null stock effects [D6p2].
The stable SDU stock — 100,800 units in 2019 rising to 111,200 in 2025, through the ordinance [D2p1]
As one think-tank piece notes, that stability may be "an artifact of a non-binding instrument" [D12p2].
The reviewed elasticity of marginal SDU-type supply is 0.31–0.48: a 10 percent cap-induced cut removes roughly 3–5 percent of stock over five years [D6p1].

Modelled for a Hong Kong-like market, a 15 percent initial-rent cut transfers about HK$900 a month to incumbents while leaving 3,000–4,000 households a year unable to enter the segment — mostly new arrivals and newly formed households [D6p4].

Berlin is the cautionary case: initial-offer rents fell, listing supply contracted within a year, and when the Mietendeckel was struck down a backlog of suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend line [D7p1][D7p2].

Berlin is the cautionary case: initial-offer rents fell, listing supply contracted within a year, and when the Mietendeckel was struck down a backlog of suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend line [D7p1][D7p2].
The tenants a cap protects are those already inside; the bill goes to those still outside [D7p3].
Inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock annually, and a band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing an estimated 40–60 staff-years [D10p1].

Worse, the tenants least able to complain — those with no written agreement, like Mrs Wong [D4p1], or the newest arrivals — are precisely the ones enforcement would miss, so a cap would "systematically miss the most exploited tail" [D10p2].

Worse, the tenants least able to complain — those with no written agreement, like Mrs Wong [D4p1], or the newest arrivals — are precisely the ones enforcement would miss, so a cap would "systematically miss the most exploited tail" [D10p2].
The subcommittee could not identify any design under which the newest-arrival tail is protected first rather than last [D10p3].
A hard cap also invites compensation claims and judicial review that would outlast a Council term [D9p1][D9p3].
A hard cap also invites compensation claims and judicial review that would outlast a Council term [D9p1][D9p3].
The NGO survey of 440 households found 61 percent would trade a nominal rent increase for three-year security of tenure, and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer [D11p1].
Mr Chan himself, offered a hard cap, named the waiting list instead: "If the queue were three years instead of five and a half, he would accept any rent to leave" [D3p3].
Second, a light indexed band on initial rents — defensible as rate-capping rather than confiscation [D9p2]
Third, redirect enforcement capacity to conditions: fire, partition, ventilation, where harm is documented and immediate [D11p2].
The deeper point is that rent caps treat the price symptom of a quantity problem: the segment is tight because the queue is long [D11p2].
Mrs Wong's confidence that landlords "would not leave the business" [D4p2]
sits awkwardly beside her own report of two flats converted to storage in her stairwell [D4p3]
— and the Association, representing 18,000 units, commits to exit if returns fall below mortgage cost [D5p2], albeit on thin, self-reported evidence [D5p3].
— and the Association, representing 18,000 units, commits to exit if returns fall below mortgage cost [D5p2], albeit on thin, self-reported evidence [D5p3].
The government's expected "floor-standard + rent band" package [D12p1]
